newsitem.title: CHINA: China copper shortfall seen 300,000 T in 2000.
newsitem.headline: China copper shortfall seen 300,000 T in 2000.

text.p: China is expected to need 1.3 million tonnes of refined copper by the year 2000, about 300,000 tonnes more than domestic supply, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

A disparity between smelting capacity and mining capacity meant China would continue to import large amounts of copper concentrate and scrap over the next few years, the newspaper quoted an official of the China National Non-ferrous Metals Industry Corp, as saying.
"China will give priority to exploring both domestic and foreign copper resources to ensure ore supplies and to upgrade major facilities," the official said.
"Efforts are now being made to ensure long-term supply contracts by investing in equipment and technologies in overseas copper mines," he said.
China has expressed interest in buying a copper mine in Chile and Premier Li Peng travelled there last month to seek an investment deal with Chilean copper producers.
New mines and refineries to be built in China in the next few years would boost copper output by 100,000 tonnes a year and help to offset the dwindling reserves of existing pits, the newspaper said.
Of China's 36 state-run copper mines, 21 pits had reserves of less than 100,000 tonnes each and 22 would have to be closed soon, it said but gave no further details.
"Poor copper ore resources have resulted in the low growth rate for copper ore production," the newspaper said.
Exploration for new reserves in large and medium-sized mines had fuelled a rise in costs, it said. The newspaper gave no further details.
China produced 745,900 tonnes of copper in January to October, up 6.66 percent compared with the same period last year, official figures show.
China's imports of uncast and raw copper jumped 28.8 percent to 549,571 tonnes between January and October.
